exercises.description: Reproduce the behavior of strncpy (man strncpy).

exercises.name: ft_str_is_alpha
exercises.description: Returns 1 if the string contains only alphabetical characters, else 0. Empty string returns 1.

exercises.name: ft_str_is_numeric
exercises.description: Returns 1 if the string contains only digits, else 0. Empty string returns 1.

exercises.name: ft_str_is_lowercase
exercises.description: Returns 1 if the string contains only lowercase alphabetical characters, else 0. Empty string returns 1.

exercises.name: ft_str_is_uppercase
exercises.description: Returns 1 if the string contains only uppercase alphabetical characters, else 0. Empty string returns 1.

exercises.name: ft_str_is_printable
exercises.description: Returns 1 if the string contains only printable characters, else 0. Empty string returns 1.

exercises.name: ft_strupcase
exercises.description: Transforms every letter to uppercase. Returns str.

exercises.name: ft_strlowcase
exercises.description: Transforms every letter to lowercase. Returns str.

post.str: Salut, Comment Tu Vas ? 42mots Quarante-Deux; Cinquante+Et+Un

exercises.name: ft_putstr_non_printable
exercises.description: Displays a string, replacing non‑printable characters by \xhh (hexadecimal, lowercase).

exercises.name: ft_strlen
exercises.description: Returns the number of characters in a string.

exercises.name: ft_putstr
exercises.description: Displays a string on the standard output.

exercises.name: ft_putnbr
exercises.description: Displays an integer.

exercises.name: ft_atoi
exercises.description: Converts the initial portion of a string to int, handling whitespace, signs, and base 10.

exercises.name: ft_putnbr_base
exercises.description: Displays a number in a given base. Handles negatives. Invalid base prints nothing.

exercises.name: ft_atoi_base
exercises.description: Converts a string in a given base to int, following the same rules as ft_atoi. Invalid base returns 0.

exercises.name: ft_iterative_factorial
exercises.description: Returns the factorial of nb (iterative). Invalid argument returns 0.

exercises.name: ft_recursive_factorial
exercises.description: Returns the factorial of nb (recursive). Invalid argument returns 0.

exercises.name: ft_iterative_power
exercises.description: Returns nb^power (iterative). Power < 0 returns 0. 0^0 returns 1.

exercises.name: ft_recursive_power
exercises.description: Returns nb^power (recursive). Power < 0 returns 0. 0^0 returns 1.

exercises.name: ft_fibonacci
exercises.description: Returns the n-th Fibonacci number (index starting at 0). Recursive. Negative index returns -1.

exercises.name: ft_sqrt
exercises.description: Returns the integer square root of nb if it exists, else 0.

exercises.name: ft_is_prime
exercises.description: Returns 1 if nb is prime, 0 otherwise.

exercises.name: ft_find_next_prime
exercises.description: Returns the smallest prime number greater than or equal to nb.

exercises.name: ft_ten_queens_puzzle
exercises.description: Displays all possible placements of ten queens on a 10x10 board (each solution as 10 digits) and returns the number of solutions (724).

exercises.name: ft_print_program_name
exercises.description: Program that displays its own name.

exercises.name: ft_print_params
exercises.description: Program that displays its given arguments, one per line, in the same order, excluding argv[0].

exercises.name: ft_rev_params
exercises.description: Program that displays its given arguments in reverse order, one per line, excluding argv[0].

exercises.name: ft_sort_params
exercises.description: Program that displays its given arguments sorted by ASCII order, one per line, excluding argv[0].

exercises.name: ft_strdup
exercises.description: Returns a pointer to a new string which is a duplicate of src, allocated with malloc.

exercises.name: ft_range
exercises.description: Returns an array of ints containing all values between min (included) and max (excluded). Returns NULL if min >= max.

exercises.name: ft_ultimate_range
exercises.prototype: int ft_ultimate_range(int **range, int min, int max);
exercises.description: Allocates and assigns an array of ints containing all values between min (included) and max (excluded) to *range. Returns the size, or -1 on error. If min>=max, *range is NULL and returns 0.

exercises.name: ft_strjoin
exercises.description: Concatenates all strings in strs separated by sep. If size is 0, returns an empty string.

exercises.name: ft_convert_base
exercises.description: Converts nbr from base_from to base_to. Returns a newly allocated string. Invalid base returns NULL.

exercises.name: ft_split
exercises.description: Splits str using any character in charset as separator. Returns a NULL-terminated array of strings. Empty strings are skipped.

exercises.description: Applies function f to each element of tab in order.

exercises.name: ft_map
exercises.description: Applies f to each element of tab and returns a new array of results.

exercises.name: ft_any
exercises.description: Returns 1 if any element of tab (NULL-terminated) makes f return non-zero.

exercises.name: ft_count_if
exercises.description: Returns the number of elements in tab (size length) for which f returns non-zero.

exercises.name: do-op
exercises.description: Program that performs an operation on two numbers. Uses an array of function pointers.

exercises.description: Sorts the NULL-terminated array tab in ASCII order by swapping pointers.

exercises.name: ft_advanced_sort_string_tab

exercises.name: ft_create_elem
exercises.description: Creates a new list element with the given data and next = NULL.

exercises.name: ft_list_push_front

exercises.name: ft_list_size
exercises.description: Returns the number of elements in the list.

exercises.name: ft_list_last
exercises.description: Returns the last element of the list.

exercises.name: ft_list_push_back
exercises.description: Adds a new element at the end of the list.

exercises.name: ft_list_push_strs
exercises.description: Creates a new list from strs. The first element is at the end of the list.

exercises.name: ft_list_clear
exercises.description: Frees all links of the list using free_fct on the data.

exercises.name: ft_list_at
exercises.description: Returns the n-th element (0-based) or NULL if not found.

exercises.name: ft_list_reverse
exercises.description: Reverses the order of the list (pointers only, not data).

exercises.name: ft_list_foreach
exercises.description: Applies function f to each element's data.

exercises.name: ft_list_foreach_if
exercises.description: Applies f to elements where cmp with data_ref returns 0.

exercises.name: ft_list_find
exercises.description: Returns the first element where cmp with data_ref returns 0.

exercises.description: Removes all elements where cmp with data_ref returns 0, freeing data with free_fct.

exercises.description: Applies applyf to each node's item using prefix traversal (root, left, right).

exercises.name: btree_apply_infix
exercises.description: Applies applyf to each node's item using infix traversal (left, root, right).

exercises.name: btree_apply_suffix
exercises.description: Applies applyf to each node's item using suffix traversal (left, right, root).
